rules.title: California Civil Code section 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just cause)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without stated just cause (at-fault or no-fault). For no-fault terminations the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months of occupancy; relocation equal to one month's rent for no-fault terminations, paid within 15 calendar days of notice
rules.penalty: Notice is void for noncompliance; actual damages, attorney's fees, up to three times actual damages for willful acts, and punitive damages; injunctive relief by the Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel
rules.status_basis: Section is in the California Civil Code; the text refers to July 1, 2020 and July 1, 2022 (mobilehome) dates, but no effective date is stated for the section itself.

exempt_if.text: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.
Residential real property alienable separate from the title to any other dwelling unit

exempt_if.name: owner_not_REIT_corporation_or_LLC_with_corporate_member_and_notice_given
exempt_if.text: Owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and tenants were given written exemption notice
Single-family owner-occupied residence in which no more than two units or bedrooms are rented
Two separate dwelling units within a single structure, owner occupies one at start of tenancy, neither is an ADU

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: Owner occupied one unit as principal residence

exempt_if.name: affordable_housing
exempt_if.text: Housing restricted by deed or regulatory agreement as affordable housing, or subject to a housing subsidy agreement

exempt_if.name: special_housing
exempt_if.text: Transient and tourist hotels, nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and residential care facilities, school dormitories, and housing sharing bathroom or kitchen with the owner

exempt_if.name: local_just_cause_ordinance
exempt_if.text: Property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective one adopted later

coverage.summary: Applies to residential tenancies of tenants who have lived in the unit for 12 months or more.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts housing under 15 years old, certain single-family homes and condos with non-corporate owners, owner-occupied small properties, affordable housing, hotels, care facilities, dormitories, and property covered by a local just cause ordinance.

precedence.text: This section does not apply to residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended after that date that is more protective than this section, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
